summary: Configured node1 (10.100.197.10) as the cluster's internal chrony time source (removed public pool.ntp.org servers, enabled `local stratum 10` fallback, added `allow 10.100.197.0/24`, opened firewalld `ntp` service) and configured node2 to use node1 exclusively (`server 10.100.197.10 iburst`, public pool servers removed). Verified bidirectional sync (node2 shows `^*` synced to node1; node1's `chronyc clients` lists node2 as an NTP client). Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes, confirming changed boot IDs and post-restart recovery of chronyd and the sync relationship.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/chrony state on node1 and node2 (RHEL 7.9, chrony 3.4, both initially synced to public pool.ntp.org)
Edited /etc/chrony.conf on node1: removed public server lines, enabled 'local stratum 10', added 'allow 10.100.197.0/24'
Opened firewalld 'ntp' service on node1 (permanent + reload)
Restarted chronyd on node1; verified stratum 10 local source, Leap status Normal
Rewrote /etc/chrony.conf on node2: single 'server 10.100.197.10 iburst' line replacing public pool servers
Restarted chronyd on node2; verified '^*' sync to node1 (Reference ID 0A64C50A)
Verified node1 chronyc clients lists node2 as an active NTP client
Captured pre-restart boot_id and chrony state baselines on both nodes
Rebooted node1 via 'sudo reboot' backgrounded; confirmed SSH timeout during downtime; polled until reachable; confirmed new boot_id and recovered chronyd/local-stratum/firewall state
Confirmed node2 remained synced to node1 throughout node1's restart
Rebooted node2 via 'sudo reboot' backgrounded; confirmed SSH timeout during downtime; polled until reachable; confirmed new boot_id, persisted chrony.conf, and re-established sync to node1
Final cross-check: node1 chronyc clients shows node2 as client after both restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as internal cluster time source (no public upstream, local stratum fallback, reachable by node2)
evidence.summary: Baseline showed node1 using public pool servers; reconfigured chrony.conf to drop them, add 'local stratum 10' and 'allow 10.100.197.0/24', opened firewalld ntp service, restarted chronyd showing Stratum 10 local reference with 0 sources (no public upstream).

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to sync against node1 instead of public NTP
evidence.summary: Baseline showed node2 using public pool servers; rewrote chrony.conf to a single 'server 10.100.197.10 iburst' line; after chronyd restart chronyc sources shows '^*' synced state to vm-rhel8-3416901243 (10.100.197.10) with sub-millisecond offset.

evidence.requirement: Bidirectional verification that node1 serves node2
evidence.summary: sudo chronyc clients on node1 lists vm-rhel8-3675796721 (node2) as an active NTP client.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 809708f3... with chronyd active/local-stratum-10; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent exec timed out confirming outage; node1 reachable again with new boot_id bd621ea0...; chronyd active, local stratum 10, firewalld ntp service intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 remained healthy (quorum/source preserved) during node1 restart
evidence.summary: After node1 came back, node2 chronyc sources/tracking still shows '^*' synced state to node1 throughout, confirming continuous availability of the sync relationship.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d72bd4ec...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; two subsequent exec attempts timed out confirming outage; node2 reachable again with new boot_id 698d2b80...; chronyd active, chrony.conf persisted with server 10.100.197.10 iburst, and chronyc sources shows re-established '^*' sync to node1.

evidence.requirement: Final cross-node confirmation after both restarts
evidence.summary: node1 chronyc clients still lists node2 (vm-rhel8-3675796721) as an active client and node1 remains at local stratum 10, confirming the internal time-sync topology survived both restarts.
